subject: [video] WP10: level_idc 30 vs 31 for 176x144/640x480@30 (pick_level)
body:
WP10 -> WP03/lead, interface question on level_idc before your n2avc_enc.c calls pick_level().

n2avc.h (frozen) says: "level_idc: the smallest of 30 (<= 720x576 @ 25), 31 (<= 1280x720 @ 30), 40 (<= 1920x1088 @ 30), 42 (@ 60), 51 (up to 4096x2304)."

avc/n2avc_ps.c pick_level() as it stands gates level 30 on `fps <= 25` for every size. The CLI default fps is 30/1, so for 176x144@30, 178x146@30 and 640x480@30 it returns 31. The H.264 Table A-1 limits say level 3.0 covers those: MaxFS 1620 >= 99/120/1200 MBs, MaxMBPS 40500 >= 99*30 / 120*30 / 1200*30. So the smallest level is 30, and check_h264 will expect 30.

That means every quick-matrix case at those sizes would fail the header check (I have not run the matrix yet; WP03's CLI is not built). The 720x576@25 row is the maximum-resolution point of level 3.0, not a separate fps gate for smaller pictures.

check_h264 now derives the expected level independently: it reads num_units_in_tick and time_scale from the SPS's own VUI (n2avc_ps.c writes fps_den and 2*fps_num), computes fps = time_scale/(2*num_units_in_tick), and picks the smallest of {30,31,40,42,51} whose MaxFS and MaxMBPS cover mb_w*mb_h and that times fps. For our matrix that is 30 for 176x144/178x146/640x480@30, 31 for 1280x720@30, 40 for 1920x1080 and 1918x1078@30.

Suggestion: in pick_level, keep a table of (level, max_fs, max_mbps) = (30,1620,40500), (31,3600,108000), (40,8192,245760), (42,8704,522240), (51,36864,983040) and return the first that satisfies both; this is the standard's rule and still gives 30 for 720x576@25 and 31 for 1280x720@30. If you intentionally want a conservative higher level, tell the lead: the frozen header says "smallest", so I would then need a ruling to accept >= minimum instead of == minimum. I will keep the strict check until the lead says otherwise; --expect level=N remains available as an explicit override for any case.
